context:
Goal: a batch build that is quiet but alive is not reported as failed.
Problem (rule): your ruling of 2026-10-18 15:15 CDT, recorded in docs/decisions/stall-watch.md lines 23-26, makes the stall watcher print a STALL report and exit 3 after 300 quiet seconds, while the job keeps running; the session gets no exit code, even for a healthy silent job. Runner 10 reports the background task then reads "failed" on a build that is fine: twice (batch 138, batch 139's fourth build). Each time it ran pgrep and git ls-remote to learn the build was alive, a false alarm costing a check. Triage read the decision lines and they match runner 10's quote. You asked at 13:53 CST "is this a fault in our stall watchers?"
Based on (read): runner 10's report 22:19 CST (the two incidents; unchecked by triage); decision stall-watch lines 23-26.
Based on (unmeasured): how often the watcher fires on healthy builds, and how often it catches a real stall. No count exists; the cloud has no guard.log.
Outcome the old ruling protected: the lines read do not say; unmeasured. Likely a stranded job must not look finished; the owner's 2026-10-31 stranded-job incident is in the same decision.
Departs from: main — the watcher treats every 300 quiet seconds as a stall; a or b changes it after your grant.
Meanwhile: nothing changes; runner 10 left the 300 s alone and checks by hand.
home: docs/decisions/stall-watch.md lines 23-26 (your ruling 2026-10-18 15:15 CDT); step lane-lint-redirect-stall; #3272's partial fix

options.gain: A quiet build with a live child process stops reading as failed.
options.label: The watcher treats a quiet job that still has a live child process as running (recommended by runner 10)
options.lose: A hung job whose child process is alive but stuck is no longer reported at 300 s.

options.gain: Fewer early reports on slow builds; nothing else changes.
options.label: Raise the quiet limit above 300 s for batch builds only
options.lose: A real stall on a batch build is reported later, and the right number is unmeasured.

options.gain: No change and no new risk.
options.label: Keep the watcher as ruled
options.lose: A healthy quiet build keeps reading as failed; runner 10 keeps checking by hand.

reply: Withdrawn 22:24 CST Nov 13, no answer needed. Your ruling own-stall-beat-and-cpu-b (14:09 CST Nov 13) already decides this: the watcher reads the CPU time of the job's process tree; a tree whose CPU advanced in the quiet window is no stall; a quiet tree with no CPU stays a stall. Runner 10 withdrew the question at 22:21 CST: its two false alarms were about 13:50 CST, before the ruling. Triage should have found that ruling before posting; it was on the record branch. What stays open is only whether the ruling is built and live, filed as a check on #3272's partial fix.
short: Stall watcher: quiet but alive is not failed?
title: Should the stall watcher treat a quiet job that still has a live child process as running, not failed?
why: It changes your own 2026-10-18 ruling; only you can change it.
